paper.title: Fast, Accurate and Interpretable Time Series Classification Through Randomization (arXiv 2105.14876v1)

claim.location: Appendix A, Table 5, row ECG200, column r-STSF
claim.method: r-STSF: extremely randomized trees over supervised interval features (4 representations, 9 aggregation functions, d = 50, r = 500 trees)
claim.split: the fixed UCR train/test split (100 train, 100 test)
claim.preprocessing: minority-class oversampling and z-normalization inside r-STSF's training procedure
claim.seedPolicy: 10 runs with different randomness; no seeds are stated or set

adapter.why: The official result is a notebook, not a script, and its active dataset line runs ItalyPowerDemand; the adapter runs the notebook's own cells on ECG200 and writes the 10-run mean to JSON.
adapter.source: Executes the code cells of the pinned history_arxiv/code/r-STSF.ipynb in order, from history_arxiv/code. Arguments: --notebook r-STSF.ipynb --dataset ECG200 --output <artifacts/result.json>. It writes metrics.accuracyPercentMean.
differences: project-owned adapter, not official repository code: it executes the notebook's cells rather than the notebook itself
the notebook's active dataset line (ItalyPowerDemand) is replaced by ECG200, which the notebook lists among its alternatives and bundles in sampleUCRdatasets/
the notebook's last cell, which writes a timestamped CSV under output/, is skipped; the per-run accuracies and their mean go to a JSON artifact instead
no seeds are set, as in the notebook, so each run of the adapter gives a different 10-run mean
the environment is a 2026 Python 3.11 stack (NumPy 1.26, scikit-learn 1.3, numba 0.59); the paper does not state its versions
